title: Larkspur Queue Service: Deployment and Operations Guide

headings.text: Larkspur Queue Service: Deployment and Operations Guide

key_sentences: Larkspur is the internal message broker used by the billing, notification and audit services.
Each production cluster runs three brokers, and every partition is replicated to all three of them.
The broker reads a single YAML file at start-up and does not reload it while running.
Upgrade one broker at a time and wait until the cluster reports all partitions in sync before moving to the next one.
If an alarm is not listed here, page the on-call engineer through the usual escalation channel.

rows: Address and port on which the broker accepts client connections.
Directory for segment files. It must be on local storage, never on a network share.
Largest accepted message in bytes. Larger messages are rejected with error LQ-413.
How long acknowledged messages are kept before compaction.
Number of brokers that hold a copy of each partition.
When a write is confirmed: leader, quorum or all.
Retention too long for the current traffic, or a consumer group has stopped.
Check consumer lag first. Lower retention.hours only after agreement with the service owner.
A broker is down or its network is saturated.
Check broker status; if a broker is down, follow the restart runbook RB-17.
Ask the producing team to split messages; do not raise the limit above 4 MB.
Open a ticket with Storage Engineering and attach the iostat output.

list_items.text: A host from the queue-node image, version 2026.09 or later, with:
at least 8 CPU cores and 32 GB of memory;
a dedicated NVMe volume of 500 GB or more for the data directory.
Membership of the lqs-operators group, which grants access to the lqsctl command.
An open change ticket for any work on a production cluster.
Drain the broker so that it stops leading partitions:
run the drain command shown below;
confirm in the dashboard that its leader count has dropped to zero.
Stop the service and install the new package.
Start the service and check its status.
Wait for re-synchronisation, then repeat from step 1 for the next broker.

furniture: Larkspur Queue Service · Operations Guide · Rev. 3.2
code:
# /etc/larkspur/broker.yaml
broker:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:7420
  data_dir: /var/lib/larkspur
  max_message_bytes: 1048576
  retention:
    hours: 72
    max_disk_gb: 400
replication:
  factor: 3
  ack: quorum

$ lqsctl broker drain --id 2 --timeout 300s
$ sudo systemctl stop larkspur-broker
$ sudo dnf install larkspur-broker-3.2.1
$ sudo systemctl start larkspur-broker
$ lqsctl broker status --id 2
